about: Lesson 7 (What does electricity cost to make?): inputs of the levelized-cost calculator and the tornado chart, and the settings of the 'when the energy arrives' step. All money is in real 2025 dollars (no inflation inside the calculation). The calculator leaves out taxes, tax credits, depreciation, interest during construction, transmission and degradation, so its results are not the agencies' own LCOE figures.

wind.design: onshore wind, EIA's capacity-weighted average of 2024 regional costs

finance.waccNote: 4% real: a round value inside the 2025 ATB's range, about 3.0-4.3% real (5.6-6.5% nominal after tax for renewables, 6.9% for gas, 2.5% inflation). Range 2-7%: illustrative.
finance.lifeNote: 30 years: the cost recovery period in both the 2025 ATB and EIA's AEO2026 levelized costs. Range 20-40 years: illustrative.
finance.blendNote: Debt at 5% and equity at 10% (nominal) are illustrative; inflation 2.5% is the 2025 ATB's assumption.

fuel.gasNote: $3.85/[[mmbtu|MMBtu]]: average cost of gas to U.S. power plants in 2025. Range $2.40-$7.21: illustrative bounds in 2025 dollars, set at the 2020 and 2022 averages without adjusting for inflation.

tornadoRanges.note: Building cost and fixed upkeep: plus or minus 25%, illustrative.
tornadoRanges.gasNote: Gas $2.40-$7.21 per MMBtu: illustrative bounds in 2025 dollars.

blindspot.about: Prairie Town's summer peak-demand day: the 2025 summer day with the highest hourly demand on the Southwest Power Pool grid (town_days.json, from EIA-930). Demand = shape x 450 MW (lesson 0's scale), wind = shape x 150 MW, solar = shape x farm size, each rounded to whole MW. Each hour, one more MWh saves the running cost of the most expensive plant still needed (town.json, illustrative): $0 if wind and sun are already being spilled, $40 if the combined-cycle plant is the last one running, $100 if the peaker is. A plant's value per MWh is the output-weighted average of those hourly values (a marginal value, not the total cost a whole farm avoids); its output counts all MWh it could make, spilled or used.
